company_name: Southern Cross Media Group Limited (Southern Cross Austereo)

inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report: share-based payment expense A$2.562m (cash-flow reconciliation, AR line 4871, and statement of changes in equity). No equity-award tax line (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 throughout). The company also spent A$1.965m buying shares on market for the executive plan. 0.23% of statutory revenue, 0.14% of 12-month pro forma revenue; the forward path uses 0.15%.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 478.779m ordinary shares on issue at 30 June 2026 (239.899m legacy SCA + 238.880m issued to SWM holders on 7 January 2026) plus 3.717m performance rights outstanding (FY2026 AR note 6.4C). Held flat because SBC is expensed in the flows. The Metrics CSV SharesOutstanding column (368.570m) is the FY2026 WEIGHTED AVERAGE, which straddles the merger, and must not be used forward; the year-end count is in SharesIssuedPeriodEnd.
inputs.fy0: FY2026 (12-month pro forma revenue base; statutory FY2026 for owner FCF and balance sheet)
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-13 ASX regular close (Yahoo daily bar; the chart-meta regularMarketPrice lags at the 9 Nov print, so the latest daily bar is used)
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD flows, AUD-built rate: ~4.4% Australian 10-year government bond + ~6% ERP x a levered beta of ~1.3-1.4 gives a cost of equity near 12.5%; bank debt at ~7.5-8% pre-tax (5.5% after tax); at a 50/50 target capital structure (the market-value structure is more debt-heavy, which would give a lower figure) WACC is ~9-9.5%. 9.5% is used in ALL three scenarios: the risks (ad-market decline, leverage, integration, governance) are charged in the scenario flows and the bear weight, not a second time in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Lease cash (principal + interest) is charged in the flows through lease_cost_pct_path and the A$289.9m of lease liabilities is EXCLUDED from net debt. Anchor: A$38.3m of total lease payments on the 12-month pro forma basis (FY2026 results presentation cash-flow slide; A$43.1m in FY2025), and A$37.8m contractually due within one year (AR note 4.3B) = 2.1% of year-1 revenue. Statutory FY2026 lease cash was A$26.2m (14.1 principal + 12.1 interest) because it holds only half a year of SWM. D&A paths are ex right-of-use depreciation (statutory ROU depreciation A$17.4m, about A$26m on a 12-month basis).
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interests; SWM was acquired 100%.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon, with the non-US adaptations (AUD WACC, single lease treatment, non-operating assets in the bridge). Routed as an operating company: an advertising-funded TV/radio/publishing group whose value is a stream of free cash flow. Not a takeover or distressed case -- the merger has completed, the facility is refinanced with no maturity before July 2029 and the stock trades normally. THIS IS AN UPDATE of the 2026-11-15 first build, which used web-research estimates because the FY2026 annual report was not on disk; it now is, and every anchor is read off it (see reconciliation). BASE-YEAR CHOICE: statutory FY2026 (revenue 1,108.3, EBITDA before significant items 134.9, net loss 13.1, FCF -5.3) consolidates SWM only from 23 December 2025 -- about 27 weeks of a business that is three-quarters of the group -- and carries A$29.9m of significant items. It is the correct record of what happened and is used for last_fcf, the balance sheet and the historical series, but compounding a growth path from 1,108 would understate the company's revenue by 40%. The forward build therefore starts from the 12-MONTH PRO FORMA basis, which is no longer an estimate: revenue A$1,869.6m is the AASB 3 as-if-acquired-on-1-July disclosure in the audited acquisition note (AR note 7.5), and EBITDA A$191.9m excluding onerous-contract releases reconciles to statutory in the results presentation (134.9 statutory + 65.1 SWM pre-acquisition - 8.1 onerous release). last_fcf is statutory and is NOT the projection base; the component build is. EBITDA MARGIN PATHS ARE CASH-ADJUSTED AND EX-ONEROUS: (1) ex-onerous means the full contracted cost of loss-making sports/programme contracts is borne in the flows each year, so the A$84.5m onerous-contract provision is NOT deducted in the bridge (that would charge it twice); statutory EBITDA will read roughly A$30m a year higher than this basis while the provision is utilised. (2) a further cash haircut of 2.0pp in year 1, 1.8pp in year 2 and 1.6pp thereafter (bull 1.3pp, bear 2.0pp) for cash that EBITDA never becomes: the company's own pro forma cash-flow bridge shows non-cash items of A$20-21m a year excluding onerous (deferred-income unwind, contra) and A$19-21m a year of redundancy and restructuring cash in BOTH FY2025 and FY2026. SBC is ~0.15% of revenue, so house and street values nearly coincide and band_position carries no information. Buybacks: none since FY2023; a 4.0c final FY2025 dividend (A$9.6m) was paid in H1 FY2026, none since, DRP suspended. The price is a regular-session close, not an after-hours print.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Face value: gross borrowings A$505.0m less cash A$142.2m = A$362.8m, the figure the company reports as net debt excluding unamortised borrowing costs. The balance-sheet carrying amount of borrowings is A$500.6m (net of A$4.4m capitalised costs), which gives the A$358.4m quoted in the annual report text; the face amount is what is owed. Lease liabilities excluded (charged in flows).

equity_bridge.note: Contracted cash sale for A$11m agreed June 2026, completion expected Q1 FY2027 (FY2026 AR note 4.5, balance sheet 'Assets held for sale').

equity_bridge.note: A$17.634m at 30 June 2026 after a A$17.7m fair-value write-down taken through OCI in FY2026 (AR note 4.5). Dividend income from these (A$0.2m) is immaterial. Equity-accounted investees (A$18.4m) are NOT added because their share of profit (A$0.9m) sits inside EBITDA.
A$17.197m of lease make-good cash due within 12 months as offices are exited (AR note 4.4). Not in lease payments, not in EBITDA. The non-current A$16.0m is left out as a recurring end-of-lease cost.

historical_growth.basis: Statutory, FY2023->FY2026 and FY2021->FY2026. Revenue 504.3 / 528.6 -> 1,108.3; equity 435.1 / 642.5 -> 363.3. Owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC; interest income not stripped because the group is in net debt): FY2021 102.0, FY2023 31.8, FY2025 54.9, FY2026 -7.8. FCF and EPS CAGRs are undefined because the FY2026 end values are negative.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: pro forma revenue mix (linear TV/radio/print ~83% declining mid-single digits, digital ~17% growing ~10%); NOT a historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-6% to -11%) and revenue CAGR (+16% to +30%) diverge by far more than 30 points and neither is a growth signal: the revenue jump is the scrip acquisition of SWM (half a year consolidated), paid for by doubling the share count, while equity reflects A$1.3bn of cumulative impairments partly offset by A$190m of shares issued. On a like-for-like 12-month basis revenue FELL 4.5% in FY2026 (1,958.2 -> 1,869.6). None of the historical rates is a valid forward anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF and reported FCF are nearly identical through history because SBC is under 0.25% of revenue. FY2025 operating cash flow was restated from 65.4 to 52.0 (interest paid reclassified into operating); the series above keeps the original basis for continuity, so FY2025 owner FCF on the restated basis is about 41.5.

base.rationale: Revenue (unchanged from the prior build): FY2026 pro forma fell 4.5%; Q1 FY2027 trading is TV flat against a market down mid-single digits, audio up low single digits, publishing stable, helped by the Commonwealth Games and AFL finals, so year 1 is -2%, then -3% as the event tailwind lapses, easing toward -1% as digital (17% of revenue, +11%) becomes a larger share. Margin (re-judged for years 1-2, haircut widened throughout): on the ex-onerous basis FY2026 was 10.3%. Management guides FY2027 total operating expenses to GROW, below inflation, with one-off Commonwealth Games and Rugby League World Cup costs and the A$145-150m cost programme only 'substantially delivered by end FY27'; on revenue of -2% that arithmetic gives EBITDA of roughly A$150-180m, so year 1 is 9.0% as reported (A$165m), 7.0% after the 2.0pp cash haircut. Year 2 gets the full run-rate savings and loses the event costs: 10.6% reported, 8.8% cash. Years 3-10 keep the prior build's reported path (peak ~12%, drifting to 11% as linear decline and rights escalators absorb about two-thirds of the savings) less a 1.6pp haircut instead of 1.0pp. Capex 1.5% rising to 1.8% (pro forma FY2026 A$27.5m = 1.47%, FY2025 A$35.4m = 1.8%). D&A ex right-of-use 3.3% (pro forma 88.3 less ~26 ROU) converging to capex by year 10 so the purchase-price step-up is not capitalised as a perpetual tax shield. Cash tax ramps from the low rates paid recently (pro forma A$13.4m, sheltered by interest and TV production rebates) to the 30% statutory rate -- unchanged. Working capital zero. Terminal: zero growth, capped at 10x FCF; the cap binds.

bull.rationale: Digital (7plus, LiSTNR, The Nightly) keeps growing 10%+ and offsets linear decline so revenue stabilises by FY2029; roughly half of the A$145-150m cost programme is retained. Year 1 still carries the event costs and partial-year savings (9.9% reported, 8.1% cash on flat revenue = EBITDA ~A$185m); the reported margin then reaches 15% by FY2030 as in the prior build, 13.7% after a 1.3pp cash haircut (prior 1.0pp). Still below the 19% SWM earned on its own in FY2022.

bear.rationale: FTA TV advertising keeps falling near 10% a year, digital growth slows, and fixed sports-rights and lease costs cannot be cut as fast as revenue. Year 1: revenue -5% against opex that management itself expects to grow gives a reported margin near 7.3% (5.3% cash). The cost programme lands in year 2 (9.0% reported) and is then fully absorbed; the reported margin erodes to 7% as in the prior build, 5.0% after a 2.0pp cash haircut because restructuring is continuous in this path. Lease cash is roughly fixed in dollars so it rises as a share of shrinking revenue; capex likewise.

scenario_narratives.base: A managed decline with a one-off cost reset. Free-to-air TV advertising, about two-thirds of revenue, keeps shrinking mid-single digits; radio is flat; 7plus, LiSTNR and The Nightly grow about 10% but are only a sixth of the group. FY2027 is a trough year for margin: operating costs still rise because of the Commonwealth Games, the Rugby League World Cup and contracted rights growth, while the A$145-150m cost programme is delivered through the year rather than at its start. The programme is real but mostly defensive: it lifts the reported margin to about 12% by FY2029 before linear decline and AFL/cricket escalators take it back to 11%. Roughly A$30m a year of reported EBITDA never becomes cash (deferred-income unwind, contra, recurring redundancy). Unlevered owner FCF runs about A$55m in FY2027 and A$75-80m a year after that, against A$363m of net bank debt whose first maturity is July 2029 -- enough to service and slowly repay, not enough to make the equity safe.
scenario_narratives.bull: The merger thesis works. A single TV + audio + publishing buy wins share from Nine and Ten (Seven already took share in FY2026 and Q1 FY2027), digital revenue outgrows the linear decline every year as it did for the first time in FY2026, and roughly half of the cost programme reaches the bottom line. The new CEO (Rohan Lund) and sales leadership settle, and the AFL contract, already held to inflation after its FY2026 step-up, stops being a margin headwind. Revenue stabilises around A$1.85-1.9bn and reported margins recover to 15%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The advertising market does the work the bear case always feared: metro FTA TV keeps falling near 10% a year, national advertisers keep leaving regional radio, and A$1.65bn of committed programme and sports-rights purchases (A$337m due within a year) stays fixed while revenue shrinks. The savings that arrive are swallowed. Cash margins fall to 5%, unlevered free cash flow falls below the interest bill, and the discounted flows are worth less than the A$363m of bank debt -- the per-share value is negative, meaning the equity is worth nothing on this path without new capital. The covenants (net leverage below 3.25x, interest cover above 3.0x, first tested December 2026) are comfortable today at 1.8x but would come under pressure around FY2029, which is also when the facility matures: this is the dilutive-recapitalisation scenario.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: UNCHANGED from the prior build (30/50/20). Bear held at 30%, double the house default: net bank debt is 1.8x reported pro forma EBITDA on a business whose largest segment is in structural decline, FY2026 guidance was cut twice, and leadership turned over within weeks of completion. Base 50%: a slow decline cushioned by cost-out is what the FY2026 result and Q1 FY2027 trading show. Bull 20%: it needs digital growth, cross-sell, cost retention and stable leadership together. What would move them: a clean December 2026 covenant test with FY2027 EBITDA tracking above A$180m would cut the bear weight toward 20-25%; a guidance cut or covenant amendment would raise it.

valuation_philosophy.summary: SXL today is a different company from the one in its history: legacy SCA radio is under a quarter of revenue, and the acquired Seven West Media business (TV, 7plus, publishing) is the rest. Statutory FY2026 -- revenue A$1,108m, EBITDA A$134.9m, a A$13.1m loss, free cash flow of -A$5.3m -- is the true record of the year but is not a run-rate, because SWM is in it for 27 weeks and A$29.9m of merger and restructuring items run through it. The model therefore keeps statutory figures for everything that is a stock or a record (net debt, shares, last_fcf, history) and builds the forward flows from the audited 12-month pro forma revenue of A$1,869.6m and the reconciled ex-onerous EBITDA of A$191.9m. It does not take that EBITDA at face value: the company's own cash-flow bridge shows only A$41m of pre-financing cash on A$200m of EBITDA in FY2026 and A$87m on A$234m in FY2025, so the margin path is cut by 1.6-2.0 points for cash that never arrives, and FY2027 is modelled as a trough because management guides costs up, not down, in that year. The question the model answers is how much of the EBITDA survives a shrinking linear ad market after leases, capex, tax and A$363m of net bank debt. Equity is a thin, geared slice of enterprise value, so small changes in margin move the per-share value a lot: the scenario spread is wide by construction and the bear case leaves nothing for shareholders. Risk is charged through the scenario flows and a 30% bear weight, with one 9.5% WACC throughout and a 10x terminal cap that reflects a structurally declining medium.
valuation_philosophy.base_year_anchor_decision: Run-rate (12-month pro forma) for the FLOW base, statutory for STOCKS and HISTORY. Rejected alternatives: (a) statutory revenue 1,108.3 as base_revenue -- understates the ongoing business by 40% and would need a fictitious +69% year-1 growth rate to correct; (b) annualising the consolidated half -- SWM's first half is seasonally larger (760.6 pre-acquisition vs 679.5 post), so doubling H2 understates revenue by about 8%; (c) statutory EBITDA margin 12.2% -- flattered by a full year of 23%-margin audio against half a year of 9%-margin TV, and includes the onerous-provision release. The pro forma figures are labelled as such wherever they appear.
valuation_philosophy.structural_discontinuity_handling: (1) Forward revenue base is the audited as-if-combined FY2026 figure (AR note 7.5). (2) Historical CAGRs are reported on the statutory series and flagged as non-predictive. (3) Share count is the post-merger year-end count plus performance rights, not the weighted average in the CSV. (4) Net debt is the 30 June 2026 balance at face value. (5) Leases are charged once, in the flows. (6) Onerous contracts are charged once, in the flows (ex-onerous EBITDA), not again in the bridge.
valuation_philosophy.unchanged_from_prior_build: Deliberately left alone, with what would move each: revenue growth paths in all three scenarios (a full half of FY2027 trading or FY2027 guidance); WACC 9.5% (a change in the debt margin or a re-rating of sector betas); terminal growth 0 / +1 / -1.5 and the 10x cap (evidence that digital revenue exceeds linear decline for several consecutive years); cash-tax ramp 15% -> 30% (disclosure of usable tax losses or production-rebate scale); lease-cost path (further space compression); SBC 0.15%; scenario weights 30/50/20; reported-basis EBITDA margins for years 3-10; hurdle 15%.
key_risks_to_valuation: Operating leverage on a geared equity: one point of EBITDA margin is ~A$18m a year, roughly A$0.20-0.25 per share of value against a share price under A$0.50.

FY2027 margin is the single most uncertain input. Guidance is qualitative ('operating expenses to grow below inflation'); the modelled 9.0% reported margin (EBITDA ~A$165m) sits below FY2026's A$191.9m. If the cost programme lands earlier and FY2027 EBITDA holds near A$190m, base value rises by roughly A$0.10 a share.

Cash conversion: pre-financing cash was 21% of EBITDA in FY2026 and 37% in FY2025 on the company's own bridge. The model assumes working-capital outflows (A$29m and A$13m) stop and restructuring cash halves; if they persist the 1.6pp haircut is too small.

Sports and programme rights: A$1.65bn of commitments (A$337m within a year, A$1.18bn in years 1-5), several times the market capitalisation, and an A$84.5m onerous provision that says some are already loss-making. Renegotiation is upside; escalators against falling revenue are the bear case.
Covenants: net leverage below 3.25x and interest cover above 3.0x, first tested for December 2026. Reported leverage is 1.8x; the bear path breaches around FY2029.
Purchase-price accounting is still provisional (12-month window to December 2026); goodwill, provisions and investments may be restated.
The bear value is negative and is carried into the weighted value at its negative figure. Flooring it at zero (limited liability) would lift the weighted value by about A$0.13 a share.
Not modelled: up to A$23.8m BAI transmission termination fee from 2030 (A$3.8m provided), the A$3.0m Network Ten profit-share receivable, A$16.0m of non-current make-good provisions.
Governance: new CEO and chair in 2026, Seven Group-associated holders owning a large block after the scrip merger.
